summary: Q-SYMBIO (25282031; 420 patients, oral CoQ10 300 mg/day for 2 years, adjunct to standard therapy) halved the primary long-term MACE composite (HR 0.50) while 16-week co-primary endpoints were null. The 2024 meta-analysis (39462324; 32 RCTs) found lower all-cause mortality (RR 0.64) and HF hospitalization (RR 0.50) in oral trials, with largely unclear risk of bias. Credit is scoped to adjunctive chronic heart failure (Dr. Pham's held scope); statin-myopathy and energy claims are excluded. Fourth-ruling boundary applied: supported outcome narrowed to adjunctive heart failure; energy, statin, muscle-pain and healthy-adult heart-health positioning excluded.

applicability.studied_population: Adults with chronic heart failure taking CoQ10 as an adjunct to conventional heart-failure therapy. Not energy, statin-myopathy relief, or cardiovascular prevention in healthy adults.

identity.preparation: Oral CoQ10 (ubiquinone; one ubiquinol trial) adjunct to conventional heart-failure therapy; the single nasal-drop trial (Mareev 2017) did not report mortality or hospitalization

population.description: 32 RCTs, 3763 heart-failure patients (1898 CoQ10, 1845 control) on conventional therapy; 22 trials in Asia; placebo used in 12 trials, conventional therapy alone in the rest. Abstract states 33 studies.

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of RCTs (PROSPERO CRD42023493184); primary outcomes all-cause mortality and HF hospitalization.

outcomes.name: All-cause mortality (11 trials, 2070 participants): RR 0.64 (95% CI 0.48-0.85), p=0.002, I2=0%; GRADE moderate
Hospitalization for heart failure (3 trials, 1034 participants): RR 0.50 (0.37-0.67), p<0.00001, I2=0%; GRADE moderate
LVEF MD 0.51, 6MWT MD 31.70 m, NYHA MD -0.29, BNP MD -91.97 (GRADE low to moderate)

limitations: Only 6 of 32 trials reported randomization methods and 3 allocation concealment; most were open-label versus conventional therapy alone (placebo in 12). Risk of bias largely unclear.
Abstract states 33 studies; body and Table 1 enumerate 32 RCTs/3763 patients. Discrepancy retained, not reconciled.
Oral regimens in Table 1 range from 30 mg/day (10 mg three times daily) to 400 mg/day ubiquinol; heterogeneous durations (3 weeks to 26.5 months). No pooled dose threshold.
Adjunctive heart-failure context only; no statin-myopathy, general energy or healthy-adult transfer (returned decision).
The mortality and hospitalization pools include Q-SYMBIO (25282031); this context and the Q-SYMBIO context are not independent replications.

study_contexts.study_design: Q-SYMBIO: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter 2-year trial (ISRCTN94506234); intention-to-treat analysis.

outcomes.name: Primary long-term composite MACE (time to first event) at 2 years: 15% CoQ10 vs 26% placebo, HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.32-0.80), p=0.003
Primary short-term endpoints at 16 weeks (NYHA class, 6-minute walk, NT-proBNP): no significant changes
Cardiovascular mortality 9% vs 16% (p=0.026), all-cause mortality 10% vs 18% (p=0.018), HF hospital stays lower (p=0.033); NYHA improved at 2 years (p=0.028)

limitations: Full text is not open access; only the PubMed abstract was retrieved in this session. Dose, duration, n and endpoints are from the abstract; physical dosage form and exact NYHA entry criteria were not verifiable here.

Adjunctive to standard heart-failure therapy only; does not establish CoQ10 as replacement therapy, nor statin-myopathy, general energy or healthy-adult cardiovascular benefit (Dr. Pham's returned decision rejects statin-myopathy and universal-energy transfers).
Co-primary short-term endpoints were null; the positive finding is the long-term composite. Phase II single trial; replication of hard outcomes rests on small pooled trials.
300 mg/day is the tested regimen, not a minimum effective dose.
